This writ petition has been filed to direct the 4th Respondent to take appropriate action on petitioner representation dated 06.12.2023 2.

Mr.P.Sathish, learned Additional Government Pleader, takes notice on behalf of the respondents 1, 3 & 4 and Mr.Abishek Murthy, learned Government Advocate, takes notice on behalf of the 2nd respondent.
3. By consent of the parties, the main writ petition is taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in this case, the subject land of the petitioner was acquired by the 4th respondent.

Thereafter, upon receipt of information with regard t o t h e c o m p e n s a t i o n a s c e r t a i n e d b y t h e 4 t h r e s p o n d e n t , t h e p e t i t i o n e r h a d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 07/10/2025 07:14:37 pm ) requested them to refer the case to the competent Court.

Accordingly, the case was referred in LAOP No.678/03, 62007,
621/07, which were settled and the compensation was fixed at a sum of Rs.4,000/- per cent.
Aggrieved over the same, an appeal was preferred by the 4th respondent before the Hon'ble Apex Court, whereby, the aforesaid compensation of Rs.4,000/- per cent was confirmed.
Pursuant to the same, the compensation was settled to the petitioner.
However, after the receipt of said amount, the petitioner found that an extent of 2.27 cents out of 14.25 cents was omitted to be referred.

Therefore,
a representation dated 06.10.2023 was filed before the 4th respondent to refer the omitted portion to the Competent Court.
However, the said representation was not considered by the respondent till date.
Hence, this petition.

5. In reply, the learned Additional Government Pleader and the learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent would request this Court to grant 4 weeks time for considering the representation of the petitioner.
